title: Descent and coherence of smooth comparisons for ordinary resolution towers
statement:
Fix a totally ordered set $L$. Let $\mathcal C$ be the reduced finite-type $\mathbf Q$-schemes admitting a closed embedding into a smooth separated finite-type scheme, including finite disjoint unions [def-pc-reduced-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-closed-immersion, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Suppose $A$ assigns to every $X\in\mathcal C$ a finite ordinary regular resolution tower with distinct increasing labels in $L$, coherent nonempty nowhere dense regular centers, and regular last level [def-trf-ordinary-resolution-rule, def-nagata-global-blowup, pqf-def-coherent, def-weil-regular-scheme]. For every smooth map in $\mathcal C$, assume that the source tower is canonically the contracted cartesian pullback of the target tower, with identical retained labels and extended center ideals [def-pc-fibre-product, def-nagata-extended-ideal]. Contraction deletes precisely unit-ideal stages. Suppose $R$ assigns regular towers with the same labeling convention to all reduced finite-type $\mathbf Q$-schemes and, for every finite affine cover $U=\coprod_a U_a\to S$, has a canonical identification $R(S)\times_S U\simeq A(U)$ with no deleted labels. Assume these identifications are the ones obtained by gluing the equal labeled ideals on overlaps and are independent of cover with the cover-comparison cocycle [def-weil-open-immersion].

Then every smooth $h:T\to S$ has a canonical contracted cartesian comparison $R(T)\simeq(h^*R(S))^c$, preserving the original order of labels and the extended ideals. For any finite affine cover $U=\coprod U_a\to S$ and finite affine cover $V=\coprod V_b\to T$ subordinate to the opens $h^{-1}U_a$, this comparison restricts to the specified comparison for the induced smooth $V\to U$. A global stage is deleted exactly when its extended ideal is unit on every lifted $V_b$; at each retained stage its ideal equals the ideal of $R(T)$ under the comparison. The comparisons are independent of the subordinate covers and have cartesian squares at every level.

For identity maps the retained-stage maps, counts and level maps are identities. For composable smooth maps $Z\xrightarrow{g}T\xrightarrow{h}S$, the comparison for $h\circ g$ equals the composite of the two comparisons, including the level maps and the ordered deletion data, with the canonical cartesian associativity identifications. On every affine blowup chart these level identifications are the canonical tensor base-change identifications. If $h$ is surjective, no stage is deleted. These statements allow varying relative dimension and apply to finite disjoint unions as whole inputs. If $A(\varnothing)$ is trivial, then $R(\varnothing)$ is trivial.

proof.text: For each smooth rational map h choose a labeled comparison c_h together with its restrictions to every subordinate cover by [lem-trf-affine-cover-ordinary-resolution-comparison]. The assigned towers and their regularity are exactly D.tower and D.tower.regular, so no new tower data are chosen.

Injectivity of the label order embeddings gives r_id(k)=k and r_hg(k)=r_h(r_g(k)). A count is determined by its value zero, its after-retained equations and its deleted-level equations, by induction on the original finite level. For the composite candidate c_g(c_h(i)), a stage absent from r_h has unchanged c_h; a stage in r_h but absent from the composite is deleted by r_g. These two cases prove the deleted equations and hence the count composition law. The identity count follows directly from the identity survivor equation and count_after.

The tower transition-to-base equations follow from transition_comp. For the identity, the index-transport identity map and c_id.levelMap have the same base composite, so [lem-trf-ordinary-resolution-level-map-rigidity] identifies them. For a composite, the transported composite of c_g.levelMap and c_h.levelMap has the base composite of c_hg.levelMap, by their cartesian square equations; rigidity identifies these maps. This constructs the smooth-functorial ordinary rule and pins it to D.tower with its original labels.

For a retained step k and any permitted isomorphism of blowups over the lower source level, form the right side of CanonicalSteps with the published blowupFlatBaseChangeIso. Its composite with the old blowup map is the new blowup map followed by the lower map: use the pullback condition and blowupFlatBaseChangeIso_hom_snd. The specified blowup_fac equations and the lower cartesian square then identify its composite to S with that of the upper levelMap. Apply rigidity, with the count_after transport. This proves precisely the canonical-step equation, without needing a separate affine tensor-chart restriction theorem.

The support of an extended ideal is the inverse image of its support. Therefore an ideal is unit if and only if its restriction to every lifted source-cover member is unit: for the reverse implication, lift any supposed support point through a cover member using the scheme pullback point-existence theorem and obtain a contradiction. Combine this with c_h.deleted_iff_unit. If h is surjective, each levelMap is surjective by its cartesian square and surjective base change; a nonempty center has nonempty inverse image, so its extended ideal is not unit and every stage survives.

A positive-length regular tower over an empty input would have a point in its first nonempty center, and its toBase map would give a point of the empty scheme. Thus its length is zero, independently of the local tower. Assemble the rule, the restrictions, local deletion, survivor laws, canonical steps and empty-input equation into DescendedRule.

split_report.summary: Proved the conditional descent theorem in nine steps. Reused the existing ordinary flat blowup comparison, its tensor chart formula, scheme-morphism gluing, smooth restriction/locality and flat/surjective base-change nodes. The proof constructs one globally synchronized survivor list from A on a disjoint union, glues level isomorphisms, and checks cover independence, all index data, identity, composition, surjective nondeletion and the empty case. No new nodes and no statement changes.
